title: Legacy Studio-only script disposition matrix
evidence_level: source-proven only; nothing here is Studio or runtime evidence

coverage.scope_note: The place held 290 scripts. 262 were already represented by canonical repository source and the import recorded them as 'canonical repo wins'; those are not Studio-only and are out of scope here. The 28 unique_files entries are the complete Studio-only set.
coverage.coverage_rule: Every path in the import manifest's unique_files must be classified by exactly one entry. Enforced by scripts/validate_migration_manifests.py.

classifications.CANONICAL_REPLACEMENT: A canonical system already owns this responsibility. The legacy module is superseded outright and must never boot beside its replacement.
classifications.REUSABLE_LOGIC_CANDIDATE: Contains behaviour or tuning worth porting into a canonical owner, after it is made deterministic, bounded and server-authoritative.
classifications.CONTENT_ONLY_REFERENCE: Data, not behaviour. Useful as design input; carries no logic worth porting.
classifications.DEAD_OR_STALE: Not worth carrying forward. Either trivially replaceable or out of authorized scope.
classifications.REQUIRES_MANUAL_STUDIO_INSPECTION: Cannot be classified from the repository because the source was lost with the damaged archive and no reference copy survives.

entries.summary: Prefix/suffix affix table and per-rarity affix budgets for item generation.
entries.canonical_representation: Affix identity, stat targets and roll ranges become data behind the deterministic item-generation rules of BA-043. EliteAffixResolver already owns enemy elite affixes and must not be conflated with item affixes.
entries.runtime_gate: integration; no item-generation activation before BA-043's gate
entries.notes: Rarity budgets (Common 1.0x/0 affixes through Mythic 4.5x/3 prefixes + 2 suffixes, plus a separate Corrupted 3.5x tier) are the most directly reusable part. Affix ids are lowercase and stable, which makes them safe to reference as content ids.

entries.summary: Room-type weights and a single prototype dungeon layout descriptor.
entries.canonical_representation: Room sequencing is already owned by the Expedition room stack. Use the legacy weights as tuning reference for BA-030/BA-032 content, not as a second room model.
entries.notes: Only one dungeon was ever defined ('prototype_dungeon', 5-8 rooms, 2-4 enemies per room, secret room enabled). Weights normal 50 / combat 30 / loot 15 with boss and secret at 0 are useful pacing evidence for the first repeatable expedition.

entries.summary: Legacy RPG enemy roster with stats, behaviour tags and reward references.
entries.canonical_representation: Enemy identity and behaviour already belong to EnemyConfig/EnemyContracts under EnemyDirectorService authority. Treat the legacy roster as archetype coverage input for BA-040.
entries.notes: Useful as a foil for BA-040: the legacy roster distinguishes melee chase, ranged and tiered (Normal/Elite/Boss) pressure with explicit detectionRange, attackRange and attackCooldown, which is exactly the archetype-coverage vocabulary BA-040 needs. Theme is medieval (goblin, skeleton) and does not match the canonical setting.

entries.summary: Legacy weapon, armor, consumable and material catalog.
entries.canonical_representation: Canonical equipment and inventory contracts own item identity. The legacy catalog is design reference for BA-024 vendor stock and BA-042 loot coverage.
entries.notes: Item ids are referenced by LootTables and by the legacy vendor path, so this file is the join key for the legacy economy. Do not import the ids into canonical content without deciding whether the medieval item set survives the setting reconciliation.

entries.summary: Weighted per-source loot tables with gold ranges, material and item rolls.
entries.canonical_representation: Canonical loot config and resolvers own drop decisions. Legacy tables are tuning reference for BA-042.
entries.notes: The table shape (goldRange, materialChance, weighted materials, weighted items, guaranteedDrops, dropChance) is a reasonable model, but a 0.15 item dropChance with 0 guaranteed drops is the kind of tuning BA-042 should evaluate against build decisions rather than copy.

entries.summary: Central RNG tuning: rarity weights, luck scaling, corruption chance, dungeon/world/boss modifier tables.
entries.canonical_representation: A canonical, frozen config behind the seedable item-generation resolver of BA-043, following the table.freeze pattern the other shared configs use.
entries.notes: The highest-value recovered config at 15,128 bytes. Luck-weighted rarity (base weights Common 1000 down to Mythic 1, plus LuckMultiplier 0.5 per luck point) and a separate 3% Corrupted roll with a per-level ramp are a coherent build-decision system with no canonical equivalent. Canonical use must make the seed explicit rather than relying on ambient randomness.

entries.summary: Damage-type, enemy-tier and combat-event string enumerations.
entries.canonical_representation: Canonical combat contracts already declare strict Luau types and reason ids.
entries.notes: Despite the 'Types' path these are runtime string tables, not Luau type declarations, and the file is not strict-mode. The seven-element damage-type set (Physical/Fire/Frost/Lightning/Poison/Shadow/Holy) is the only content worth noting, and it belongs to a fantasy damage model the canonical game does not currently use.

entries.summary: Rarity, equipment-slot, item-type and damage-type string enumerations.
entries.canonical_representation: Canonical equipment and inventory contracts own slots and rarity vocabulary.
entries.notes: Duplicates the damage-type table from CombatTypes, which is exactly the kind of drift a single canonical contract prevents. The nine-slot equipment layout is useful reference for BA-042 build-decision breadth.

entries.summary: Player data defaults, experience curve, level-from-experience conversion and luck handling.
entries.canonical_representation: The experience curve is a pure formula worth evaluating for BA-044. The persisted data shape must not be revived; PlayerInventoryContracts is canonical and persistence is gated by Phase D.
entries.runtime_gate: integration; persistence remains blocked by Phase D regardless
entries.notes: expForLevel is floor(100 * level^1.5 + (level-1) * 50) and levelFromExp iterates it; the iteration is unbounded, so a corrupt or hostile total would spin. Any canonical port needs a bounded closed form or an explicit cap. The 'luck' stat is the hook the whole legacy RNG system hangs on and has no canonical counterpart.

entries.summary: Round, clamp, lerp, map and approach math helpers.
entries.canonical_representation: None. Canonical modules use math.clamp, math.floor and inline interpolation directly.
entries.notes: Adding a shared math utility would create new surface for no behavioural gain, and math.clamp already exists. Kept only so the import stays complete.

entries.summary: Central RNG engine: luck-modified rarity rolling, dungeon/world/enemy/boss modifier generation, quest generation.
entries.canonical_representation: A pure, seeded resolver in src/shared that takes an explicit RNG and returns copied results, testable through Lune exactly like the existing Expedition resolvers.
entries.notes: Its own header lists LootService, DungeonService, EnemyService, CombatService and RPGServerBootstrap as callers, so this module is the shared spine of the legacy RPG. Blocking defect for a straight port: every entry point defaults to `rng = rng or Random.new()`, so omitting the seed silently produces non-reproducible results. Canonical use must require the seed.

entries.summary: Seeded random helpers: weighted selection, gaussian, shuffle, chance, multi-roll.
entries.canonical_representation: The weighted-selection and shuffle primitives BA-043 needs, rewritten in strict Luau with a required RNG argument and no mutation of caller-owned tables.
entries.notes: Two defects not to carry over: `RandomUtility.choice(table, rng)` names its parameter `table`, shadowing the global inside the function, and `shuffle` mutates and returns the caller's table, which conflicts with the canonical rule that pure resolvers return copies. The same `rng or Random.new()` fallback as RNGEngine applies here.

entries.summary: Legacy monetization service.
entries.canonical_representation: None. A broad monetization catalog is explicitly unauthorized by the master roadmap's scope protection, and no canonical monetization owner exists.
entries.runtime_gate: blocked; out of authorized scope and additionally guarded by BA-071
entries.notes: Marked archive_only_do_not_boot by the import. Any future monetization work starts from product decisions and real product ids, not from this module. Recovered bytes are retained only so the import stays complete.

entries.summary: Legacy RPG server entry point that wired combat, enemies, inventory, loot, player data and the hub together.
entries.canonical_representation: None. The canonical server bootstrap fully replaces it.
entries.runtime_gate: blocked permanently; booting this beside the canonical bootstrap is a named stop condition
entries.notes: At 25,700 bytes this is the largest preserved script and the single most dangerous one to revive: it would start a second combat, enemy, inventory, loot and persistence stack. It also requires AbilityDefinitions, HubTownConfig and HubTownContracts, none of which existed in the place, so it could not have run there either. BA-071 adds the source audit that fails if it is ever wired in.

entries.summary: Legacy server combat resolution.
entries.canonical_representation: None. Canonical combat authority is complete and covered by existing fixtures.
entries.notes: Marked archive_only_do_not_boot by the import.

entries.summary: Procedural dungeon generation: rooms, corridors, secret rooms, modifiers and encounter placement.
entries.canonical_representation: Fold ideas into the existing Expedition room stack as BA-030/BA-032 content. The module itself is archive: the canonical stack already owns room sequencing, placement and secret branches.
entries.runtime_gate: blocked; ideas only, no second generator
entries.notes: 18,508 bytes and the richest reusable service. Marked preserved_unique_reference rather than do-not-boot, but it still must not run beside ExpeditionRoomPlacementService. A normalized readable copy is also exposed at imports/studio-2026-08-07/readable-reference/ServerScriptService/Services/DungeonService.luau; the recovered byte-exact copy is authoritative.

entries.summary: Legacy enemy spawning, state and behaviour.
entries.canonical_representation: None. EnemyDirectorService is the canonical enemy authority.
entries.notes: 23,660 bytes, marked archive_only_do_not_boot. Its behaviour vocabulary is already captured through legacy.config.enemy-definitions for BA-040, so the module itself carries no further value.

entries.summary: Legacy hub service: rotating vendor stock, daily deals, rarity upgrades, purchases and NPC interaction.
entries.canonical_representation: Vendor behaviour re-expressed as a deterministic resolver over canonical inventory and currency authority. Fully specified in the BA-001 manifest entry hubtown.script.hub-town-service.
entries.notes: Byte-exact source lost. A normalized readable copy survives at imports/studio-2026-08-07/readable-reference/ServerScriptService/Services/HubTownService.luau, which is enough to classify it and extract its concepts, but not enough to call it preserved. Cross-referenced by docs/migration/hubtown-migration-manifest.json.

entries.summary: Legacy inventory management.
entries.canonical_representation: None. Canonical inventory owns item ownership, session leases and dismantle rules.
entries.notes: Source lost, but the classification is safe: the import already marked it archive_only_do_not_boot and a canonical replacement exists with fixture coverage. Nothing depends on reading it.

entries.summary: Legacy loot rolling and drop delivery.
entries.canonical_representation: None. Canonical loot resolvers and services own drop authority.
entries.notes: Source lost. Its tuning survives through legacy.config.loot-tables and its RNG behaviour through legacy.utility.rng-engine, so nothing of value depends on the module text.

entries.summary: Legacy player data persistence and currency handling.
entries.canonical_representation: None. Canonical persistence owns the adapter boundary, and Phase D gates any further persistence work.
entries.runtime_gate: blocked permanently; guarded by BA-071 and additionally by Phase D
studio_only: DataStore behaviour in an appropriate test environment
entries.notes: Source lost. Reviving a legacy persistence path is doubly forbidden: it would duplicate canonical authority, and the master roadmap blocks durable persistence until runtime ownership is trustworthy.

entries.summary: Procedural short-session quest generation with modifiers and progression hooks.
entries.canonical_representation: Quest archetypes and modifiers re-expressed as canonical quest contracts with a deterministic state resolver (BA-020). No canonical quest system exists today.
entries.runtime_gate: integration; quest state stays server-authoritative and unwired until the integration gate
entries.notes: Byte-exact source lost. A normalized readable copy survives at imports/studio-2026-08-07/readable-reference/ServerScriptService/Services/QuestService.luau and is the practical input for BA-020. It is the only surviving evidence of the legacy quest model, so BA-020 should mine it before it is forgotten.

entries.summary: Resource gathering, hatchet harvesting and crafting/building.
entries.canonical_representation: Resource-node and recipe content models under BA-022/BA-023, using canonical inventory authority and server-validated interaction. Gathering remains a scope decision, not an assumed feature.
entries.runtime_gate: integration; gated additionally by an explicit gameplay-fit decision
entries.notes: Source lost, but its mechanics were extracted before the loss and survive in imports/studio-2026-08-07/readable-reference/GATHERING-CRAFTING-CONCEPTS.md: 7-stud range, 0.55s swing cooldown, 45s node respawn, 10% critical harvest, 5% rare discovery, Trees/Rocks/IronOre groups and nine recipes. The Workspace/Resources folders (Trees, Rocks, IronOre) recovered in the hierarchy index are this service's content.

entries.summary: Main legacy RPG client HUD and menus.
entries.canonical_representation: Screen and state matrix under BA-063. Any adopted layout idea must respect the canonical centralized presentation owners and accessibility config.
entries.notes: The largest lost file at 31,158 bytes, with no reference copy and no concepts document. Only its identity and size are known. BA-063 must design from the canonical loop rather than wait for it, and treat any later re-extraction as a comparison, not a source.

entries.summary: Legacy vendor/shop client interface.
entries.canonical_representation: Vendor screen defined by BA-063 against the BA-024 vendor contracts, with all purchase authority server-side.
entries.notes: Lost with no reference copy. It was the client half of HubTownService's purchase path, so whatever it displayed came from a vendor catalog that also no longer exists.

entries.summary: Legacy survival/gathering HUD.
entries.canonical_representation: Any retained gathering readout is defined by BA-063 and only if BA-023's gathering scope decision keeps the feature.
entries.notes: Lost with no reference copy. Its underlying mechanics survive through GATHERING-CRAFTING-CONCEPTS.md, so the information it displayed is inferable even though the layout is not.

entries.summary: Client-side hatchet swing controller from the legacy StarterPack tool.
entries.canonical_representation: Semantic action definitions and client-only input mapping under BA-062. A client swing may only send a narrowly scoped intent; harvest and damage resolution stay server-side.
entries.notes: Lost with no reference copy. Its timing constants survive in GATHERING-CRAFTING-CONCEPTS.md (7-stud range, 0.55s cooldown). Whether the legacy client authored harvest results cannot be checked, which is itself a reason not to port it: the canonical rule is that the client never establishes consequential truth.

entries.summary: Legacy client controller wiring input and remotes to the RPG server stack.
entries.canonical_representation: None. The canonical client entry point already owns controller startup, and BA-062 owns any input abstraction work.
entries.runtime_gate: blocked; a second client controller would duplicate canonical startup
entries.notes: Lost with no reference copy. It was the client counterpart of RPGServerBootstrap, so it is superseded by the canonical client entry point regardless of what it contained.

open_gaps.summary: Eleven of the 28 preserved Studio-only scripts have no recoverable source in the repository, so their classification rests on import-manifest identity plus, where one exists, a normalized reference copy.
open_gaps.resolution: Re-extract the 11 files listed under archives.legacy-src.unrecoverable_files in INTEGRITY-BASELINE.json, per docs/production/RBXL-IMPORT-INTEGRITY-2026-08-07.md.

open_gaps.summary: All four legacy UI/client scripts are lost with no reference copy, so 66,525 bytes of client interface behaviour is known only by file identity.
open_gaps.resolution: BA-063 designs the information architecture from the canonical loop instead of waiting. Treat any later re-extraction as comparison material rather than a source of truth.

open_gaps.summary: The legacy stack references AbilityDefinitions, HubTownConfig and HubTownContracts, which were never present in the place. Three named legacy dependencies have no source anywhere.
open_gaps.resolution: Treat them as absent by design. Do not reconstruct them from call sites; the corresponding canonical content is new design work.
